When Hitman 3 first launched in 2021, it was the first time since Absolution that I'd felt a strong urge to step into the shoes of Agent 47. The reason: its Berlin level. Set in the grimy, sweaty Club Hölle, it was the first time I'd ever seen a videogame get a nightclub right. The density of people on the dancefloor, the slight griminess that coated the whole place. The lights, the music. I didn't think another game would out-do it anytime soon. There's an awful lot to be impressed with in Rockstar's newest blockbuster—and I should hope so, considering how much money and time went into making the damn thing—but nothing has stood out to me more than Leonida's nightlife. Hitman 3 did it excellently in isolation, but GTA 6 has managed to incorporate an immersive, lively club scene right into the open world. And after spending far too much time in Vice City's Big Three—that's NINE1NINE, Jack of Hearts, and The Vault—I'm floored not only by how good a job Rockstar did of making them feel like a club you would end up inside in real life, but how distinct they all are from one another. You've got your overpriced luxury half-strip-club, half-regular-club with NINE1NINE (inspired by Miami's own E11EVEN), where a beer costs 15 goddamn bucks even after you already fork out the $150 cover charge to get in. There's the sticky, dollar bill-laden floors of Jack of Hearts where MCs belt out over the mic and the bass practically splits the speakers open.
